feature: Lens: a layer that changes what is under it
summary: Drag a box over anything with the new Lens tool and the picture underneath is drawn through it: blur an address until it cannot be read, pixelate a name, drain the colour out of a region, invert it, or lift and push its brightness. It is an ordinary layer otherwise, so it moves, resizes, turns, rounds, takes a border and a shadow, sits in the layer list and undoes.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. The flag is A layer that changes what is under it (next-lens), on by default.

try.do: Open a screenshot with some text on it.
Press K. The capsule over the tool bar should now say Lens, Blur, Strength.
Drag a box over one line of text. The words go soft and the tool hands back to Select with the lens picked.
In the panel, open Lens and change Does to Pixelate.
Pull Block size and watch the blocks change size under your finger.
Try Greyscale, then Invert, then Brightness on the same lens.
Drag the lens up onto a different part of the picture.
Pull Corner Radius in Appearance, then press Command Z twice.

evaluate: K is a letter with no meaning: is a keyboard shortcut worth having here at all, or should the lens be reached only from the tool bar?
Is Lens the right word on the tool bar, or would Blur, Hide or Redact say more to somebody who has never seen it?
The panel row reads Does: Pixelate. Does that read as a setting of the layer, or would you expect to find this in Effects?
A new lens arrives with no border and no shadow, so it looks like the picture, changed. Is that right, or should a fresh one wear a ring so you can see where it is?
Pixelate goes up to 80 points a block. Is that too coarse, too fine, or about right for a retina screenshot?
Five adjustments in one menu: is anything missing that you would reach for on a screenshot?
rough: Screen Recording was granted, so every picture here is a real capture of the window, not an offscreen render.

A ROTATED lens turns the picture it samples along with its box, so a blurred region sits at an angle to everything round it. The zoom callout has done the same since it shipped. Filed as 'A lens turned on its side still shows the picture straight'.

A zoom callout is the same idea with Magnify as its adjustment, and folding it in is the right end state, but it carries chrome outside its own frame and it is shipped, so it was left alone. Filed as 'A zoom callout becomes a Magnify lens'.

Changed from the task's own sketch: no shape enum. A lens is its box plus the corner radii every layer already has, so dragging the radius to its top gives the capsule or the circle, and there is no second control to explain.

A lens has no picture of its own, so a drag shows no floating sprite: the whole composite is redrawn each move, the same fallback the zoom callout already uses. On a 12 megapixel capture that is about 7ms a move, so it feels the same, but it is worth watching on something much bigger.

The live draft while you drag out a new lens is a thin blue hairline box, not the adjustment itself. Previewing the real thing needs the composite underneath, which is only rebuilt on release. What the draft promises is the BOX, and the box is exactly what lands.
A Brightness lens set to nought is invisible on the canvas. It is still in the layer list, but there is nothing on the picture to click.

The whole walk sweep was asked for rather than run: the lens adds one more button to the tool bar in Next, which shifts every slot after it. The toolbar, narrow-window and panel-arms walks were run by hand and all pass.
